title: Advance directive and DNACPR
stem: Resus 3. Madam Lee, 86, with end-stage heart failure and advanced dementia, has come in from her care home with pneumonia and low blood pressure. She cannot communicate. Her daughter has arrived with a folder and asks you not to 'put her through CPR and tubes'. Discuss the plan with the daughter.

review.text: The new law. Your notes list 'advanced directive' as a topic only. Hong Kong's Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance (in force 31 July 2026) gives advance medical directives and DNACPR orders legal effect, including outside hospital. Family cannot refuse treatment on an adult's behalf; they tell you the patient's wishes. Check the Hospital Authority's current forms.

notes:
Checked against Hong Kong's Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance (passed November 2024, in force 31 July 2026), the Hospital Authority guidance on advance directives and DNACPR, and the Hong Kong Medical Council Code.

The Ordinance gives legal effect to advance medical directives (AMDs) made by a mentally capable adult with an advanced, irreversible disease, meeting statutory formalities, and to DNACPR orders made by registered medical practitioners; DNACPR orders now also apply outside hospital, and rescuers act on them. The maker can revoke an AMD at any time. Clinicians are protected when they give life-sustaining treatment without notice of a valid AMD, or withhold it in the honest and reasonable belief that one is valid and applicable.

Family members cannot make or refuse treatment decisions on behalf of an adult who lacks capacity (unless appointed under a legal mechanism); they are consulted about the patient's values and wishes, and the doctor decides in the patient's best interests. Check the document: is it an AMD by the patient herself, is it valid (formalities, capacity at the time), and is it applicable to this situation? A DNACPR decision does not mean 'no treatment': antibiotics, oxygen, fluids and comfort continue unless also refused.

Your notes list 'advanced directive' as a topic without detail. The Ordinance's details (forms, witnesses) should be checked against the HA's current forms.

steps.label: Ask Ms Lee
steps.hint: What document is it, who made it, when, was she capable, what does it cover? Her mother's values.

Document.rz: 係我阿媽兩年前簽嘅預設醫療指示，嗰陣佢嘅認知障礙症仲未咁差。佢嘅家庭醫生同一個朋友做見證人。
Document.r: An advance directive my mother signed two years ago, before the dementia got bad. Her GP and a friend witnessed it.
Document.mark: Identifies the document and who made it

Document.rz: 如果佢去到病嘅末期，唔做心肺復甦，唔用呼吸機。不過佢仍然想得到紓緩照顧。
Document.r: No CPR, no breathing machine, if she's in the final stage of an illness. She still wanted comfort care.

Document.t: Was she well enough to understand it when she signed?
Document.tz: 佢簽嗰陣，精神狀態明唔明白入面嘅內容？
Document.rz: 明白，家庭醫生有寫低佢係明白嘅。
Document.r: Yes, the GP wrote that she understood.
Document.mark: Checks capacity at the time of making

Values.t: What was your mother like? What mattered to her?
Values.tz: 你阿媽係個點樣嘅人？佢最重視啲咩？
Values.rz: 佢好憎入醫院。佢話想安詳咁走，唔想插滿喉。
Values.r: She hated hospitals. She said she wanted to die peacefully, not with machines.
Values.mark: Explores the patient's values and wishes

Values.t: Has anything changed since, has she ever said otherwise?
Values.tz: 之後有冇改變過？佢有冇講過相反嘅說話？
Values.rz: 冇，佢舊年仲講多咗一次。
Values.r: No, she said it again last year.
Values.mark: Checks there is no sign of revocation

steps.label: Explain the plan
steps.hint: Validity and applicability; DNACPR is not 'no care'; comfort; honesty about prognosis.

turns.line: So will you just let her die?
turns.lz: 咁你哋係咪就由得佢死？

opts.t: No — we'll keep treating the pneumonia with antibiotics, oxygen and fluids, and make sure she's comfortable. What your mother refused was CPR and a breathing machine, and her directive is valid and applies now, so we will respect it.
opts.tz: 唔係——我哋會繼續用抗生素、氧氣同吊鹽水醫佢個肺炎，亦都會確保佢舒服。你阿媽拒絕嘅係心肺復甦同呼吸機，而佢份預設醫療指示係有效、而家適用嘅，所以我哋會尊重佢嘅意願。
opts.rz: 多謝你……呢個就係佢想要嘅。
opts.r: Thank you… that's what she wanted.
opts.mark: Explains that DNACPR does not mean withdrawing other treatment

turns.line: My brother in Canada says we should do everything.
turns.lz: 我喺加拿大嘅阿哥話要盡晒力搶救。

opts.t: I understand he's worried. Family can't override a valid advance directive — it's your mother's own decision. I'm happy to speak to him by phone to explain.
opts.tz: 我明白佢好擔心。家人係唔可以推翻一份有效嘅預設醫療指示——呢個係你阿媽自己嘅決定。我好樂意打電話同佢解釋。
opts.rz: 麻煩你可以嗎？佢會聽你講。
opts.r: Please would you? He'll listen to you.
opts.mark: Explains that family cannot override a valid AMD; offers to talk to the brother

opts.t: Then we'll do CPR to keep him happy.
opts.tz: 咁為咗令佢開心，我哋就做心肺復甦啦。

opts.t: She's very unwell. She may improve with antibiotics, but she might die in the next few days. We'll keep you updated and you can stay with her.
opts.tz: 佢而家病得好重。用咗抗生素可能會好轉，但都有機會喺呢幾日走。我哋會隨時同你更新，你可以陪住佢。
opts.mark: Gives honest prognosis and invites the family to stay

steps.label: Talk to the nurse
steps.hint: Document the decision, complete the DNACPR form, a ceiling of care, comfort measures.

opts.t: Copy the directive into the notes; complete the DNACPR form; ward ceiling: no ICU, no intubation
opts.mark: Documents the AMD and DNACPR decision clearly

opts.t: Continue antibiotics, oxygen, fluids; analgesia and mouth care; palliative care review
opts.mark: Continues appropriate treatment and comfort care

opts.r: The directive refused CPR and ventilation, not antibiotics or comfort.

qs.q: Who can make an advance medical directive?
qs.a: A mentally capable adult, for their own treatment
wrong: The GP on the patient's behalf, at a clinic visit
Any family member holding an enduring power of attorney

qs.q: When does the HK Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance take effect?
Does a DNACPR order stop antibiotics and fluids?
qs.a: No — it applies to CPR only

qs.q: Can a relative override a valid, applicable AMD?
What protection do doctors have under the Ordinance?
qs.a: Protection when acting in good faith on a valid order
wrong: None; they may still be sued for withholding CPR
Protection only if they perform full resuscitation
Protection only with a court order in each case

badge.name: Her Own Words
badge.flavor: Valid, applicable, respected. DNACPR is not 'no care'.

cards.q: An advance medical directive is valid when made by…
options: A mentally capable adult for themselves
The family, on the patient's behalf, after discussion
The treating team, by consensus
A medical social worker assigned to the family
cards.source: HK Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance

cards.q: DNACPR orders under the new HK Ordinance apply…
options: In and outside hospital
Only in intensive care units
Only inside public hospitals
Only in the patient's own home
cards.why: Rescuers act on them outside hospital too.

cards.q: The HK advance decision law came into force on…
options: 31 July 2026
1 January 2024
20 January 2026
Not yet
No CPR; other care continues
No active treatment of any kind
No nursing or comfort care at all
No antibiotics or IV fluids
cards.why: Ceilings of care are separate decisions.

cards.q: For an incapable adult without an AMD, decisions are made…
options: The doctor, in best interests, consulting family
The eldest child as legal next of kin, after a family meeting
The court, every time
A majority vote of the relatives
cards.why: Family inform, they do not decide.

options: Yes, by the maker at any time
No, it is permanent once signed
Only by an order of the court
Only by the family, acting jointly and in writing
cards.why: In the manner the Ordinance specifies.
